"Nhard raid unable to check scba"

"Everything was checked and in working order at this time was unable to do any of the check list do to heavy rain at check time"

The technician states he could not complete the checklist, yet the checklist section was submitted with values. 7. Rolando Flores (1099) — SM Energy, Money Graham CTB, trailer 148, 4:52 PM, Trailer Readiness Form. The same field reads:

8. Bryan Medlin — trailer 603, 1:41 PM, Trailer Readiness Form, filed at the Andrews shop. The same field reads:
"The mask bags and stickers were not changed due to there are not anymore in the shop"

This is a stock-out at the shop rather than a fault with the trailer, and read alongside items 2 and 3 it suggests mask bag supply is the common thread across three technicians today. No notified party is named. Follow-up: confirm shop mask bag and sticker stock and reorder.

9. Luis Zarate — XTO Energy, Q4 quarterly well testing, multiple locations, 4:27 PM, job 36571_2. Tube readings above zero were recorded at four of five sites, the highest being 100 PPM: Scott 35-34H recorded 100 PPM at both heater treater outlet samples and 100 PPM at the flare; Marienfeld 13-24H recorded 80 PPM and 100 PPM at the re-boiler; Houston Ranch 35-8H recorded 40 PPM twice at the heater treater outlet; Tom 35-42H recorded 40 PPM twice at the re-boiler. The "Comment or Issues" field was left blank at all five sites. Taking these readings is the purpose of a quarterly well test, so the readings themselves are expected data rather than an incident, but readings at that level with no comment entered leave no record of whether anything was escalated to the customer. Follow-up: confirm with Zarate whether the 100 PPM readings were reported to XTO and have the comment fields complete

clean.text: Nothing requiring attention from: Nathan Contreras (two trailer inspections and a readiness form for 272, plus his Junior Mint West air job); Ruben Rojo (two inspections and a readiness form for 139, plus two SM air jobs — only the placeholder note is against him); Humberto Marquez-Salazar (two inspections and a readiness form for 607, plus his Hoelscher air job); Larry Jaramillo (two inspections and a readiness form for 601, plus his Crespi air job); Jacob Hernandez (two inspections for 175 plus his Brook O air job, the best-documented OWL close-out of the day); Alexander Clubb (two inspections for 608); Ralph Forbes (two inspections for 605 and a complete Bates close-out); Michael Ellis (trailer inspection for 506, his daily and his Butler 5H supervision close-out — only the 2021 photo reuse is against him); Dennis Easley and Allen White (complete dailies with proper hydro and cascade

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when it was taken but not what it shows.

A second limitation specific to today: this review ran at 11:00 PM Central, an hour before the calendar day closed. The most recent submission captured arrived at 8:30 PM. Any form filed in the last hours of the day, or arriving tomorrow morning for work done today, is not in these figures. Where a form is reported as not received, that is the state of the mailbox at 11:00 PM tonight and it may yet arrive.

81 of 81 submissions read. The job board was available — Blake Walton's 11/3/2026 Ark-La-Tex and Permian Basin boards were used, and 55 manned rows were checked for coverage, 39 on the Permian board and 16 on the Ark-La-Tex board.
